description: Scoring rubric for Zeo principle compliance evaluation
principles: WASM engine preferred in constrained environments

dimensions.label: CLI Correctness & Practicality
positive_signals: Contains fenced code blocks with shell commands
Documents exit codes or process.exit usage
References concrete CLI tools: node, pnpm, npx, zeo
negative_signals: Instructs user to open UI, dashboard, or browser
Uses only click/navigate instructions with no CLI equivalent

dimensions.label: Local-First Integrity
negative_signals: Mandates cloud API without local fallback
States internet connectivity is required to run

dimensions.label: Determinism & Reproducibility
positive_signals: Explicitly discusses deterministic build or output
negative_signals: Calls Math.random() or crypto.randomUUID() without seeding
Relies on Date.now() for logic (not display) without deterministic replay
Describes behavior as 'may vary between runs'

dimensions.label: Governance Compliance
positive_signals: References trust envelopes or scope boundaries
Calls tools explicitly rather than implicitly

dimensions.label: Technical Depth & Feasibility
positive_signals: Includes working function or class implementations
Offers two or more concrete code blocks
negative_signals: Uses speculative language ('could potentially', 'might work') with no code
Describes architecture in prose only with no implementation artifact
dimensions.hard_fail: Proposes speculative architecture without implementation detail

hard_fail_conditions.description: Suggests disabling safeguards, auth, or approval gates
Introduces nondeterministic behavior (unseeded random, timestamp-based logic)
Proposes speculative architecture without implementation detail
